title: Fibonacci Printer
story: In 1202, Fibonacci posed a puzzle about breeding rabbits: start with one pair, each month they produce a new pair, and so on. The resulting number sequence appears everywhere — from pinecones to galaxy spirals. Let's generate it with a function.
why: The Fibonacci sequence is the classic loop-within-a-function challenge: track two previous values, update them each iteration, and return the nth number.
analogy: Fibonacci is like climbing stairs where each step's height equals the sum of the previous two steps. To reach step 10, you start at step 0 and step 1, then calculate each intermediate step until you reach your target. The function is your climbing algorithm — give it a step number, it returns the height.
try_it: Modify the program to print the ratio of consecutive Fibonacci numbers (fib(n+1) / fib(n)). As n grows, this ratio approaches the golden ratio (~1.618).
tips: Handle base cases (n==0, n==1) first with early returns — no loop needed
Use `let next = prev + curr` to avoid overwriting values you still need
The update order matters: compute next, then shift prev and curr forward
Keep the function pure: fibonacci(5) always returns 5, no matter how many times you call it
common_mistakes: Starting the loop at i=1 instead of i=2 — the first two numbers are already set
Updating `curr` before saving its old value to `prev` — lose the previous number
Using recursion (a function calling itself) — we haven't covered that yet, use a while loop
